Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 33-year-old non-smoking woman with known intermittent asthma presents with 2–3 days of wheeze, exertional dyspnoea and dry cough; temperature 37 °C; no chest pain or sputum; using salbutamol PRN.  

Likely diagnoses (consistent with DDx and transcript):  
• Acute asthma exacerbation – High likelihood given history and symptoms.  
• Viral respiratory tract infection / acute bronchitis precipitating asthma – Moderate likelihood.  
• Allergic (pollen-related) asthma flare – Moderate likelihood due to atopic history.  

Working diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of asthma, probably triggered by viral infection or allergens.  

Management Plan

• Increase salbutamol use to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours via spacer.  
• Prescribe spacer device; pharmacist to demonstrate technique.  
• Prescribe peak flow meter; patient to record morning and evening values for one week.  
• Recommend regular oral antihistamine (OTC) for hay fever.  
• Safety-net: return/call urgently if fever develops, wheeze worsens, or breathing deteriorates.  
• Arrange follow-up tele-review in one week to assess peak-flow readings and consider additional controller therapy.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute asthma exacerbation – High likelihood: classic wheeze/dyspnoea in known asthmatic, improvement at rest, no better alternative explanation.  
2. Viral respiratory infection / acute bronchitis – Moderate likelihood: acute onset with mild fever and cough may have precipitated flare.  
3. Allergic (pollen-induced) asthma flare – Moderate likelihood: atopic background; seasonal triggers possible despite absence of current rhinorrhoea.

● No direct contradictions between transcript and DDx; patient reported “fever” but measured temperature was normal (37 °C).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional minor ambiguities but overall adequate for history-taking.
